name: Protection / Lightsmith
note: CANONICAL, hand-edited. Generates CombatAssistPlus/Catalogs/Protection.lua via `wowkb.capart export catalog protection`, and the per-ability state table the preview draws. The Lightsmith roster; Templar is a separate catalog authored later, not a second overlay bolted on here. ⚠ `hero` is deliberately unset: the Paladin hero sub-tree ids have not been read from a live client, and inventing one would silently bind nothing. Unset means "any hero tree" — and unlike Retribution, whose roster was spec-wide, THIS roster is Lightsmith-specific, so a Templar Protection Paladin gets a catalog built around an armament row their build does not have. That is real exposure, not a formality. ⚠ NO `power` field, measured rather than omitted: the 12.1 Protection priority list carries no `holy_power` term of any kind. "Paladin ⇒ declare HolyPower" is exactly the inference the second Paladin catalog invites, and it is wrong. ⚠ NO row declares `charged`, and four of them would want to — this repo carries no Tier-1 charge count for Holy Armaments, Shield of the Righteous or Crusader Strike, and Judgment's second charge is talent-conditional. The consequence is that `capped` has no subject anywhere in this catalog. Base spell ids only: Bind unions base/override/tooltip/live into the row, so neither the Sacred Weapon nor the Hammer of Wrath transform needs a hardcoded override id.

abilities.note: The Sacred Weapon BUFF, not the cast. 432502 is the only "Sacred Weapon" id carrying Effect=6 apply-aura rows (five, all ImplicitTarget=21 target-ally, including EffectAura=468 -> Tempered in Battle), SpellMisc.DurationIndex=18 -> Duration=20000, description ending "Lasts $d." [T1 DB2 @ 12.1.0.69214, knowledge/classes/paladin/protection/abilities.md -> Spell-ID anchors]. This is what `buff.sacred_weapon.remains<6` reads. 432472 is the CAST, 432616/441590 the proc's damage and healing, 432757 name residue rendering Holy Bulwark's text. It holds NO CooldownSetSpell row anywhere and needs none: a sealed container is cap's OWN frame, filtered by includeSpellIDs and bound with SetUnit(plan.unit) (Channel.lua:768, :849).

The Consecration PLAYER aura -- "Standing in Consecration" -- and NOT the cast. All three of 188370's SpellEffect rows are Effect=6 at ImplicitTarget=1 (caster), and the Protection talent Strength of Conviction 379008 hangs its points on this id specifically [T1 DB2 @ 12.1.0.69214, abilities.md -> Spell-ID anchors]. 26573 is the cast and the CDM row (the 12 s field); 81297 is the periodic damage inside the field; 204242 is the enemy snare (ImplicitTarget=6, EffectAura=33). WARNING 188370 has Duration = -1: it is PRESENT/ABSENT only, so V19 and V20 are impossible on it and a presence band is the only available form. Like every aura subject it needs no CDM row -- the container is cap's own frame.

talents_note: Node + entry from `knowledge/classes/paladin/protection/ability-inventory.tsv` @ 12.1. ⚠ `divine_guidance` and `blessed_assurance` SHARE node 95235, and that is the fact rather than a typo: they are the Lightsmith choice node at 8,11, so exactly one of them exists on any build and the other is dead. Two markers are gated on it in opposite directions. ⚠ The key `divine_guidance` appears in BOTH families and that is legal — `Catalog.Check` keys `abilities` and `talents` in separate tables and the `talent` predicate resolves only the second. The aura is the stacking buff; the talent is whether the buff can exist at all.

entries.note: Rung 5. A PLACED cooldown: its value is set by what lands inside it, and Divine Toll's clock is the whole of that. Sealed, so the hold is a band.

states.condition: on cooldown
states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, Divine Toll within 10s or already ready
states.note: Rung 5 fires at `cooldown.divine_toll.remains<=10`, so this is the press window.

states.condition: ready, Divine Toll's cooldown BEYOND 10s
states.note: ⚠ The sense is `beyond`, and getting it backwards would invert the button. The rung FIRES at `remains<=10`, so the HOLD is the complement: Divine Toll is nowhere near, so this is not its moment. The band also reads nothing at zero remaining, which is correct here — a READY Divine Toll satisfies `remains<=10` and must not hold anything. ⚠ NO SCENARIO REACHES THIS STATE; it is declared from the marker, not observed in a walk.

entries.note: Rung 7, the spec's largest Holy Power injection, and it belongs inside Wings. ⚠ The rung has two disjuncts and only the second is authorable: the first is `buff.avenging_wrath.up`, and whether a Category-3 (TrackedBar) row raises the `aura` latch's alert edges is UNMEASURED. A latch on an unmeasured edge is a hold that may never release, so it is not authored.

states.condition: on cooldown
states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, Wings near or Righteous Protector talented
states.note: ⚠ Righteous Protector is near-mandatory and DELETES this cue: it halves Avenging Wrath's cooldown, which removes the disjunct from the priority. So on the build almost everyone plays, Divine Toll wears nothing and this is the only ready state. Stated as a hole rather than papered over with an approximation.

states.condition: ready, Righteous Protector UNtalented, Avenging Wrath within 30s
states.note: `within = 30` is the complement of `remains>30` and is correct wherever the band draws anything at all — which is not the whole 120s cooldown. ⚠ The band reads NOTHING on a ready dependency: at `remains = 0` there is no cooldown for the client to evaluate the curve against, so the hold is silent exactly where Avenging Wrath is available. An earlier note claimed correctness "across the entire 120s cooldown", which overstated it by one endpoint; the omission is safe (a hold that does not draw cannot eliminate the correct press) but it is not the same claim.

entries.note: Rung 9, the spender and the active mitigation. ⚠ Rung 9 is UNCONDITIONAL on Lightsmith by derivation rather than by reading: every term in its condition is Templar's, so with no Hammer of Light on the build the first disjunct is trivially true. The row needs no press gate at all, which is why the spender's placement is pure position — and why its one marker is about affordability instead.

states.condition: on cooldown
states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: affordable — in the scan by `scan_when`
not affordable
states.exception: Affordability is not a rung. The priority list assumes the resource is there — simc simply skips an action it cannot pay for — so this is cap re-presenting a cost, not a line of its own.
states.note: ⚠ R1's warning applies exactly: a spender whose cost is the only thing between it and a press raises no readiness edge for that cost, so Blizzard's border cannot say this. It is shown castable, it is off the global, and it is the button pressed out of habit at the wrong Holy Power. The client also tints it `not-enough-power` — that tint is Blizzard's and cap neither draws nor undoes it.

entries.note: Rungs 10 / 14, 23. One button, two jobs. ⚠ Rung 23's charge dump is not authored and the reason is the ROW ORDER, not missing data (Defeats, item 4).

markers.note: V19, and the FIRST consumer of `outside_s` in any catalog. Rung 10 is `holy_armaments,if=next_armament=sacred_weapon&(buff.sacred_weapon.remains<6|!buff.sacred_weapon.up)`, and V19's pair says both halves without cap reading either. Plenty of buff left -> the gold do-not-refresh hatch, off SetDurationText bands on the aura's remaining seconds at the catalog's own 6 (Channel.lua:625-643); inside Blizzard's refresh window -> the badge, on a window the CLIENT computes per spell. No buff at all -> no aura, no button, no sink, so the row draws nothing and is a live candidate, which is the `!buff.sacred_weapon.up` half for free. 6 is the APL's own number and is also 30 % of the buff's 20 s duration, so the hatch's edge and the client's window edge very nearly coincide -- the seam is a flight question. Gated on the SACRED WEAPON life: in the Bulwark life rung 10 cannot fire and the weapon buff says nothing about the Bulwark. That gate rests on the same open direction as cue D (fact-classification.md 5.1) -- if the identity reads the other way round, BOTH treatments land on the wrong life.

states.condition: on cooldown
states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, in its HOLY BULWARK life, Avenging Wrath beyond 5s
states.note: One button, two jobs, and which job it has right now is written only on the icon's own artwork. As Holy Bulwark it wants SAVING until Wings. ⚠ The hold stands at TWO charges as well, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight: rung 23 (`charges=2`) sits BELOW rungs 15, 16, 18 and 20-22, so a row the priority would dump at 23 is still outranked by three rows to this one's right. Releasing the hold there would put the row back at rung 14's rank. What is not authored is rung 23 itself — Defeats, item 4, rewritten.

states.condition: ready, Holy Bulwark life, Avenging Wrath within 5s
states.note: The hold releases: this is the window the bulwark was being banked for.

states.condition: ready, in its SACRED WEAPON life, no Sacred Weapon buff on the player
states.note: Rung 10's second disjunct, `!buff.sacred_weapon.up`, and it costs nothing to say: no aura means no matching aura, no button and no sink, so V19 draws neither its hatch nor its badge and the row is a clean candidate. That is the half this catalog used to call unsourced because no Category-2 row for the buff could be found — a sealed container needs no Cooldown-Manager row at all.

states.condition: ready, Sacred Weapon life, the buff up and INSIDE Blizzard's own refresh window
states.note: V19's badge — promotion ring, halo and the client-drained dial — on a window cap authors no threshold for. Rung 10's first disjunct, `buff.sacred_weapon.remains<6`, said by the client instead of by cap.

states.condition: ready, Sacred Weapon life, the buff up with 6s or more left
states.note: The pair's other state: the gold do-not-refresh hatch, drawn from a SetDurationText band table on `outside_s = 6`. ⚠ The elimination is unconditional and needs no outranker gate, which is unusual: in the Sacred Weapon life rungs 14 and 23 are dead too (both name `next_armament=holy_bulwark`), so with rung 10 false the row has NO live rung anywhere in the list and every row to its right outranks it.

states.condition: ready, Holy Bulwark life, Avenging Wrath beyond 5s, and BOTH charges banked
states.note: Written down as its own state because it is the one the Defeats section argues about. `capped(holy_armaments)` is readable here — Sense.readCapped calls C_Spell.GetSpellCharges live and never consults `ability.charged` — but the hold still stands, because rung 23 outranks nothing this row is drawn above. Defeats, item 4.

entries.note: Rungs 13 and 18. It FEELS like the top of the rotation and rung 18 is the low unconditional one, with three rungs between it and rung 13. Only Glory of the Vanguard genuinely puts it first — which is why the Vanguard term is a READABLE GATE on a sealed display, the `when`-beside-`display` shape. Without it the hatch would rule out the row in the one state rung 13 puts it first.

states.condition: on cooldown
states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, no hold applies
states.note: Rung 18, the low unconditional one, which is the ordinary press for most of a fight.

states.condition: ready, Judgment TRANSFORMED to Hammer of Wrath and ready, Vanguard absent
states.note: Rung 16 puts Hammer of Wrath above this row. Cue E.

states.condition: ready, Vanguard absent, Consecration also ready, Divine Guidance talented, its count at five or more
states.note: ⚠ The first sealed display in ANY catalog that rules out a row the aura does not belong to. Demonology's two count tables both sat on the row whose own press the count gated; here the count is Divine Guidance's, the entry is Avenger's Shield, and the statement is "the row to your right outranks this one right now". The mechanism needs nothing new — `Channel.Plan` binds `display.ability` independently of `entry.ability` — but the STATEMENT is a relationship rather than a self-test. ⚠ The direction is V16 and not V17, and that choice is the whole of whether it is honest: drawn the other way it would say "ruled out until Divine Guidance is capped", which is false. ⚠ `ready(consecration)` is a readable gate on the sealed display and it is what makes the elimination true: rung 15 is Consecration, so with Consecration swiped the APL falls to rung 18 and THIS row is the press. Without the term the band hatched the correct button.

states.condition: ready, Hammer of Wrath armed AND the Divine Guidance band drawing (Consecration also ready)
states.note: Both markers true at once. ⚠ The co-occurrence gate does not demand this pair be stated — it only pairs markers that carry a CUE, and `as_guidance_capped` carries none — so it is written down here on purpose rather than because something asked for it.

entries.note: Rungs 15, 19, 24 and 29. ⚠ Rungs 19 and 24 are now expressed on a BLESSED ASSURANCE build, as a V16 presence band on the player aura 188370 -- not as an `aura` latch, so the unmeasured Category-3 alert-edge question is bypassed rather than answered. On a Divine Guidance build they remain unmodelled, because rung 15 presses Consecration with the field up on a count cap may not read (Defeats, item 2).

markers.note: A PRESENCE band, and the only shape 188370 allows: the player aura carries Duration = -1, so it is present-or-absent and there is no remaining time on it to band or drain — the 12 s clock lives on the cast, 26573. One band at threshold 0 therefore draws for every value the aura can have, and the client's own blank when the aura is absent is the whole of the other state. That is rungs 19 and 24's `!consecration.up` read as an elimination, with no aura duration entering a Lua condition and no latch on an unmeasured row class. ⚠ GATED ON talent(blessed_assurance), which is what makes it honest rather than merely narrow. Rung 15 (`consecration,if=buff.divine_guidance.stack>=5`) carries NO `!consecration.up` term, so on a Divine Guidance build a capped count presses Consecration with the field still under you — and the count is sealed, so cap could never gate on it. On the other half of choice node 95235 rung 15 cannot exist at all. The gate is a POSITIVE talent read rather than `!talent(divine_guidance)` on purpose: same coverage, one fewer negation in the safety case, and it makes the mutual exclusion with `cons_awaits_hammer` (which requires talent(divine_guidance)) a property of the choice node rather than of an argument. ⚠ ready(crusader_strike) is the outranker term: rung 29 is an UNCONDITIONAL Consecration, so with the whole rest of the row unavailable the field-up Consecration IS the press and the hatch would eliminate the correct button.

states.condition: on cooldown
states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, no gate applies
states.note: The most-pressed button in the rotation and the one with the least visible reason — rungs 15, 19, 24 and 29 behind one identical icon.

states.condition: ready, Judgment transformed to Hammer of Wrath and ready, Divine Guidance talented, its count below five
states.note: ⚠ The complement's readable gate is what makes it TRUE, and this is the answer to Demonology's warning rather than an exception to it. Below five stacks Consecration is not eliminated in general — rung 19 presses it whenever the ground effect is down. The gate narrows the display to the one state where the low band IS an elimination: while Hammer of Wrath is armed and off cooldown, where rung 16 outranks rung 19. Outside that gate the client is never asked to paint anything. ⚠ With no Divine Guidance aura at all the table has no subject and NOTHING covers that state; the readable marker that filled it was deleted for DENSITY, not for being wrong.

states.condition: ready, its own ground effect still under the player, on a Blessed Assurance build, with the hammer row available
states.note: ⚠ A presence band rather than a count band, and V16 rather than V17: there is one band, at threshold 0, so it draws whenever the aura exists and the client's blank carries the other state. With the field up rungs 19 and 24 are dead and rung 15 does not exist on this build, so Consecration's only live rung is 29 — the last one in the list — and everything to this row's right outranks it. ⚠ It cannot co-occur with `cons_awaits_hammer`: that marker requires talent(divine_guidance) and this one talent(blessed_assurance), and they are the two halves of choice node 95235.

entries.note: Rungs 17, 22 / 16. ⚠ Rung 17 is not authored — the second-charge dump, and `charged` is undeclarable on this spec.

states.condition: on cooldown
states.exception: On cooldown. No rung expresses it — a priority list only ever says when to press, and Blizzard's swipe rules the row out before cap has an opinion of its own.

states.condition: ready, or in its HAMMER OF WRATH life
states.note: In its Hammer of Wrath life it needs nothing: it outranks the two rows to its left, and both of those wear cue E to say so.

states.condition: ready, BASE life, Blessed Assurance talented and its aura up, a hammer charge available
states.note: Blessed Assurance makes the hammer to its right worth more for exactly one cast. ⚠ The identity term is not decoration: rung 16 puts Hammer of Wrath above both hammer rungs, so the yield must VANISH while the row is transformed — otherwise the row that just earned cue E on two neighbours would stand itself down. ⚠ `ready(crusader_strike)` is the other load-bearing term: rungs 20 and 21 are both that roster row (Hammer of the Righteous / Blessed Hammer), so with every charge spent neither can fire and rung 22 — this row — is the press.

entries.note: Rungs 20, 21 / 25, 26. ⚠ Its Blessed Assurance promotion is expressed on Judgment (cue F), not here: this row does not change KIND under the buff, and a rank change within one kind is what the left-to-right scan already carries.

states.condition: ready
states.note: The filler, reached by subtraction. No cue solves anything here. ⚠ The row declares NO band on `identity` even though it is a choice node: both hammers have zero CooldownSetSpell rows, so exactly one exists on a build and reaches the Cooldown Manager permanently on 35395 — the transform is always on, and a band would encode a distinction that never varies.

entries.note: Rung 28. A Holy Power heal competing with the active mitigation for the same three Holy Power.

states.condition: Shining Light absent
states.note: The priority presses this in exactly one state: free. Without the proc the button has no place in the damage priority at all, so the hold is load-bearing the way Demonology's `db_awaits_core` is — it holds the row in EVERY other state, which is also why no `starved` marker is authored here: a second badge would say the same thing twice.

states.condition: Shining Light up
states.note: No cooldown state: Word of Glory has no cooldown of its own.

defeats_unreferenced.why: A finding about the BOUNDARY BETWEEN rows, not about one row: a sealed display may demote the row it is armed on and may never promote any row, because promotion is a comparison across rows. Its scenario spans Shield of the Righteous, Holy Bulwark, Avenger's Shield, Consecration and Hammer of Wrath in sequence, and the marker it was resolved by deleting (`cons_no_guidance`) was the common term of two such trios. Any single attribution would name one of five rows arbitrarily.

A three-hold trio, and the trio is the defeat: cue B on Divine Toll, cue D on Holy Armaments and cue F on Judgment stand together before the press lands on Blessed Hammer. No one of the three is the site — each is correct on its own row, and it is the density budget across them that is overspent. The item's own reopening note picks cue B as the candidate to delete IF a flight ever finds the state, which is a decision about the set rather than a home for the item.

entries_note: Entry order IS the authored priority, and it is the flattened `actions.default` — one list, no sub-lists and no hero fork, with four rows whose rungs straddle another row's. `Catalog.OrderCheck` reports when the player's Cooldown Manager disagrees with it.
